sections.text:
1 Quamquam titulo auctoris nomen non additum est, tamen ex argumento appa-
ret haec non, ut olim credidi, ipsius Palchi esse sed ab eo excerpta esse ex scriptore
ignoto saeculo circiter antiquiore. Aegyptius erat is (cf. supra, p. 80, v. 10) sed
Romae ut videtur (p. 117, v. 10) librum astrologicum composuit anno 379 p. C. n.
(p. 115, v. 4) quo tempore deorum cultus nondum exstinctus erat (al. 2, v. 10). —
Quae si recte statuimus, testimonium de veteribus astrologis iam (p. 80) pro-
latum non exeuntis est quintisae culi sed anni supra scripti.
sections.en: 1 Although the author's name is not added to the title, nevertheless from the argument it appears that these are not, as I once believed, by Palchus himself, but were excerpted by him from an unknown writer about a century older. He was an Egyptian (cf. above, p. 80, line 10) but at Rome, as it seems (p. 117, line 10), he composed an astrological book in the year 379 A.D. (p. 115, line 4), at which time the cult of the gods was not yet extinct (al. 2, line 10). — If we have established these things correctly, the testimony concerning the ancient astrologers already brought forward (p. 80) is not of the end of the fifth century, but of the year written above.

sections.en:
F. 136v (288v). 135. Effects of the epoch of the fixed
stars 1.
If therefore you find at a nativity the Moon applying to one of the
bright and notable stars, that is being about their equal degrees,
and especially if the Moon runs according to the same wind
as the bright star which is near her degrees [of the
Moon], they make the nativities great and bright and most conspicuous and wealthy.
Likewise also if one of the bright
stars is horoscoping or rising at the natal hour, or again perpendicularly
in the midheaven, or is found on the other angles, it renders them glorious
and authoritative and busy, and wealthy and known or formidable to cities
or countries, and especially in those countries
are glorified those born in which the bright stars are situated or co-rise
when one is born, as is appended in the
table; horoscoping therefore or midheavening almost from young
age and in their own cities they provide successes; but if on the
western angle is found one of the bright stars at the natal
hour, mostly abroad and about middle age it
renders happiness, and gives a bright marriage and inheritance of rich people,
but differences through pretexts rather of female persons;

summary.headline: Effects of Fixed Stars’ Epoch
summary.text: Chapter 135 explains how the epoch and angular positions of bright fixed stars affect nativities, especially through the Moon, horoscoping, midheaven, co-rising, and the western angle. A preceding paragraph gives the Sun’s effects in the place of children, friendships, works, and wealth; the apparatus discusses an excerpt attributed to Palchus and cites Firmicus and Kroll.
